passage:
After the big text fight with Sumit last month, we made a deal on the walk home. Looking back, it's the smartest thing we've done.
Rule one: if a message feels off, ask "what did you mean?" before replying. Rule two: if it still feels off, call. Rule three: if I'm hurt, I wait ten minutes before typing anything.
Yesterday I tested it. Sumit wrote, "why do you always pick that place?" Old me would have fired back. Instead, I put the phone down, made tea, and then wrote, "What did you mean?" He replied, "Just that it's far from my house lol."
That's it. A text is just letters on a screen. My tea was still hot.
Jasleen

qa.a: If hurt, wait ten minutes before typing anything.

qa.q: How did Jasleen feel when Sumit's reply came?
qa.a: Jasleen likely felt relieved and a little amused, since the message she almost took badly was harmless.

qa.q: Why is waiting before replying a useful habit?
qa.a: It gives time for hurt to settle, so Jasleen can ask what someone meant instead of reacting to a guess.

qa.q: What does this habit mean for Sumit?
qa.a: Sumit gets a chance to explain before being accused, which keeps small texts from turning into fights.

grounding: Shows teens agreeing to ask "what did you mean?" and call when a text feels off, and pausing before replying when hurt.

Class teacher's note, Friday
Nazia and Deepak asked to present something at the end of our life-skills period. After their text misunderstanding last month, which I watched spread across the whole class, they have made a poster called "Before You Hit Send". It lists: ask "what did you mean?"; if it still feels wrong, call; if you're hurt, pause before you reply.
Deepak explained, "We lost a week being angry about one word." Nazia added, "Now if a text feels off, we just call."
Several students laughed in recognition. I have put the poster on the notice board and plan to use it with Class 8 next term.

Dear diary, Tuesday
Kamal and I made our Text Rules today, sitting on the stairs after school. It was his idea, actually, after our fight in March. We wrote them on the back of my maths notebook:
1. Ask "What did you mean?" before getting upset.
2. If it still feels weird, CALL.
3. If hurt, wait. Don't reply fast.
We both signed it like a treaty. Kamal drew a peace sign.
And tonight I already needed it! He texted "k" when I sent him my essay. My thumb was ready to type something sarcastic. I made myself wait. Then I asked. He was just in the car with his dad. 🙈
Mehak

qa.q: Which rule helped most tonight, and why?
qa.a: Waiting and then asking what he meant, because it showed the "k" was just Kamal being in the car, not coldness.

qa.q: How might Kamal feel about the rules they made?
qa.a: Kamal seems keen and hopeful, since it was his idea and he drew a peace sign on it.

grounding: Shows two teens agreeing to ask what a text meant, call when unsure and wait when hurt, and using the habit the same night.
